$comment: Authored story source (S2 outline + S3 lines). tools/spec/build-script.ts counts words, plans timing and writes /spec/script.json. Edit this file for video #2.
title: THE DAY COUNTER
rule: Your wrist shows your remaining days, visible to everyone. Days are given by holding hands and saying 'take them'. A gift cannot be reversed.
twist: The ledger's first page: given days are spent together. The giver lives them alongside the receiver, so both wrists show the same number. Re-colours every gag: each giver ended up spending the days with the person they paid.
callback: Beat 1 'everybody is born with a number' -> beat 9 'everybody gets a number. I just made sure we had the same one.'

beats.name: HOOK
beats.visual: Slow push over Maple St, townsfolk checking their wrists.

lines.text: In this town, everybody is born with a number on their wrist.

beats.name: RULE
beats.visual: Insert on a wrist number, then two hands holding.

lines.text: It's how many days you have left. Everyone can see it.
And you can give them away. Hold hands, say "take them".

beats.name: GAGS
beats.visual: Three one-shot gags: office, street, schoolyard parking lot.

lines.text: People mostly use it for dumb stuff.
Uncle gave his boss a month for promotion. Now he's boss. Seventy-one.
Cousin gave her ex one day to watch him check his wrist.
Coach gave a stranger a year for parking. Now he runs everywhere.

beats.name: STAKE
beats.visual: Milo bragging in the schoolyard; cut to June; insert on her '4'.

lines.text: Me? I've got 4,015. Biggest number in my whole class.
I show everyone. I show the lunch lady. Twice.
Then there's my little sister, June. She's four.
Her wrist says 4. Not four years. Four days.

beats.name: ESCALATION
beats.visual: Clinic shrug; parents' near-empty wrists; clerk office.

lines.text: The doctor looks at her wrist and just shrugs.
Mom and Dad want to give, but they're almost empty.
So I go to the town clerk. She reads the rule out loud.
"You can give. You can never take back."
She looks at my number. Then at me. For a long time.

beats.name: ATTEMPT
beats.visual: Dinner table attempt; bedroom mirror practice at night; morning '2'.

lines.text: At dinner, I grab June's hands and say it. Take them.
She says, "Take what?" and steals my potato.
She's four. She doesn't get it. She thinks it's a game.
Mom cries into the gravy. Dad stares at his plate.
That night I practise the words in the mirror.
Take them. Take them. Take them.
Next morning, her wrist says 2. It didn't work. Nothing did.

beats.name: CLIMAX
beats.visual: Cold dawn dock. Hand hold. His number drains to 0, hers climbs past 4,000. Walk home alone.

lines.text: On her last day, I take her to the dock at sunrise.
Her favourite place. The ducks are already awake.
I hold both her hands. I don't let go.
I say it slow, like a teacher. "June. Take them."
And she says, "Okay."
Hers climbs past 4,000. She laughs. She has no idea.
I walk her home. Then I go to my room alone.

beats.name: TWIST
beats.visual: Bedroom wake-up; wrist reads 4,016; clerk office ledger; gag callbacks.

lines.text: Then I wake up. My wrist says 4,016. Same as June's.
The clerk opens the big ledger. Page one. Tiny print.
"Days given away are days spent together."
"You don't lose the day. You only lose it alone."
That's why Uncle never leaves the office.
Why my cousin got one more terrible date.
Why Coach jogs with a stranger every morning.

beats.name: CALLBACK
beats.visual: Wide dock, both on the pier, same number on both wrists. Hard cut to black on the last word.

lines.text: Everybody gets a number. I just made sure we had the same one.
